case.case_title: Pathiraja v. Mannaperuma, Secretary, Ministry of Public Administration and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC (FR) No. 665/2003, decided on 31 August 2004

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the denial of promotion to the petitioner for absence from work without approved leave violated Article 12(1) of the Constitution guaranteeing equality before the law and equal protection of the law.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that denial of promotion due to absence without approved leave violated his fundamental right to equality under Article 12(1).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondent argued that the petitioner failed to obtain the required prior permission for leave under the Establishments Code, and thus the denial of promotion was lawful and did not violate Article 12(1).
key_facts: The petitioner was a Senior Assistant Secretary in the Sri Lanka Administrative Service.
He went abroad for a postgraduate degree course in Scotland without obtaining prior permission from the Secretary to the Ministry of Public Administration as required by the Establishments Code.
The petitioner funded his studies personally after External Resources Department refused funding.
Upon return, the petitioner was denied promotion due to absence without approved leave.
The Establishments Code provisions (Chapter XII section 14:3:1 and Chapter XV sections 1:5:1 and 1:5:2) require prior permission for study leave abroad.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 12(1) as guaranteeing equality before the law and equal protection, but found that the petitioner’s failure to comply with the statutory leave requirements under the Establishments Code justified the denial of promotion. The court emphasized that the Establishments Code provisions have statutory force and must be followed.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner did not obtain the required prior permission from the Secretary to the Ministry of Public Administration before leaving for study abroad, which was a mandatory condition under the Establishments Code. The court held that this failure justified the denial of promotion and did not amount to discrimination violating Article 12(1).
principles_established: Statutory provisions in the Establishments Code have binding force.
Failure to comply with mandatory procedural requirements can justify adverse administrative action without violating equality rights.
Approval for leave for study abroad must be obtained from the Secretary to the Ministry of Public Administration for officers in the Combined Services.
precedents_cited: The Public Service United Nurses Union v Montague Jayawickrema, Minister of Public Administration and Others (1988) (1) SRI LR 229

outcome.holding: The court held that denial of promotion due to absence without approved leave was not a violation of Article 12(1) of the Constitution.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the petitioner’s claim of discrimination in denial of promotion. The court’s reasoning focused on whether the petitioner was treated unequally under the law, concluding that compliance with statutory leave requirements justified the administrative decision without violating equality rights.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner failed to obtain prior permission of the Secretary to the Ministry of Public Administration as required by the Establishments Code, and the court held that denial of promotion on this basis was not a violation of Article 12(1).
